title: Periodic Table & Bonding
description: Periodic trends, ions, ionic and covalent bonding, and molecular shapes.

questions.text: Which of these elements has the highest electronegativity?
questions.explanation: Electronegativity increases across a period and up a group. Fluorine (about 3.98 on the Pauling scale) is the most electronegative element.

questions.text: Select ALL compounds that contain ionic bonds.
questions.explanation: Ionic compounds join a metal to a nonmetal: $\ce{NaCl}$, $\ce{MgO}$ and $\ce{CaF2}$. $\ce{CH4}$ and $\ce{CO2}$ contain only nonmetals and are covalent.

questions.text: Write the formula for magnesium nitrate.
questions.explanation: Magnesium is $\ce{Mg^{2+}}$ and nitrate is $\ce{NO3-}$. Two nitrate ions are needed to balance one magnesium ion: $\ce{Mg(NO3)2}$.

questions.text: Atomic radius generally decreases from left to right across a period.
questions.explanation: Across a period the nuclear charge increases while electrons are added to the same shell, so the electrons are pulled in more tightly and the radius shrinks.

questions.text: Match each molecule to its molecular geometry (VSEPR).
questions.explanation: $\ce{CH4}$ has 4 bonding pairs (tetrahedral). $\ce{NH3}$ has 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair (trigonal pyramidal). $\ce{H2O}$ has 2 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs (bent). $\ce{CO2}$ has two double bonds and no lone pairs on carbon (linear).

questions.text: How many electrons are in one chloride ion, $\ce{Cl-}$? (Chlorine has atomic number 17.)
questions.explanation: A neutral chlorine atom has 17 electrons. The chloride ion has gained one electron, so it has 18.

questions.text: Which molecule contains a triple bond?
questions.explanation: Each nitrogen atom needs three more electrons, so two N atoms share three pairs: $\ce{N#N}$. $\ce{O2}$ has a double bond, $\ce{Cl2}$ a single bond, and $\ce{CO2}$ has two C=O double bonds.

questions.text: How many valence electrons are available in total for drawing the Lewis structure of $\ce{CO2}$?
questions.explanation: Carbon contributes 4 valence electrons and each oxygen contributes 6: 4 + 6 + 6 = 16.

questions.text: Which ion has the same electron configuration as the noble gas neon?
questions.explanation: Neon has 10 electrons. $\ce{Na+}$ (11 − 1 = 10) matches. $\ce{Cl-}$ and $\ce{K+}$ both have 18 electrons (argon), and $\ce{Li+}$ has 2 (helium).

questions.text: Write the formula of the sulfate ion, including its charge.
questions.explanation: Sulfate is a polyatomic ion with one sulfur, four oxygens and a 2− charge: $\ce{SO4^{2-}}$.
